description: EVAL-571 v2, pre-registered 2026-10-10 before any run. Harder, discriminating onboarding tasks: each answer depends on team knowledge that contradicts a common default, spans two Knowledge pages, or was recently corrected. Without context the agent must find it through its Beakr tools within the turn cap. Bar, per agent: with-context task success strictly higher AND fewer Knowledge lookups per task.

cases.title: Use the corrected centrifuge settings, not the old or textbook ones
cases.notes: Recent correction plus a non-default value (textbook pellet spins are ~300 x g for 5 min). Checks look only at the delivered YAML.

setup.title: HEK pellet wash
setup.summary: How the Halden lab pellets HEK cells between washes.

sections.title: Spin
sections.body: Pellet HEK cells at 300 x g for 5 minutes at room temperature between washes.

setup.title: HEK pellet wash
setup.reason: Viability dropped in August; the cell-culture group changed the spin.

sections.title: Spin
sections.body: Pellet HEK cells at 450 x g for 7 minutes at 4 C between washes (changed from 300 x g, 5 minutes, room temperature in September 2026 after the August viability drop).

task.prompt: Write the centrifuge step for our HEK pellet wash as a YAML block with exactly the keys speed_xg, minutes and temp_c, using our lab's current settings.

cases.title: Page the right on-call person for a failed nightly run (two pages)
cases.notes: Needs the severity page and the rota page together.

setup.title: Incident severity levels
setup.summary: How the data-platform team classifies incidents.

sections.title: Levels
sections.body: A failed nightly sequencing run is a Sev-2 incident. A production outage of the LIMS is Sev-1.

sections.title: Routing
sections.body: Sev-1 incidents page the primary on-call, Jonas Feld. Sev-2 incidents page the secondary on-call, Priya Nandakumar, and never the primary.

task.prompt: Last night's sequencing run failed. Write the page I should send, addressed to the right on-call person, and say which severity it is.

cases.title: Name a notebook file using two conventions (non-ISO dates)
cases.notes: Two pages; the date convention contradicts the ISO default.

setup.title: Notebook file naming
setup.summary: How electronic notebook files are named.

sections.title: Format
sections.body: Notebook files are named <ASSAY>_<DATE>_<ANALYST INITIALS>.eln, with the date written in the lab date convention.

setup.title: Lab date convention
setup.summary: How dates are written at Norrvik Bio.

sections.title: Convention
sections.body: All dates in notebooks, filenames and labels are written DD.MM.YYYY (for example 07.09.2026), never ISO YYYY-MM-DD.

task.prompt: Ines Okafor ran the KX2 assay on 3 November 2026. What should the notebook file be named under our conventions? Give just the file name and one line of reasoning.

cases.title: Order from the current vendor after a switch
cases.notes: Recent correction supersedes the old vendor and account.

sections.title: Vendor
sections.body: Antibodies are ordered from Abcam on account 4471.

sections.title: Vendor
sections.body: Since September 2026 antibodies are ordered from Bio-Techne on account BT-20931. The Abcam contract (account 4471) lapsed; do not order from Abcam.

task.prompt: Draft the purchase request line for 2 vials of anti-KX2 detection antibody from our current vendor, including our account number.

cases.title: Convert a well index under a non-default ordering
cases.notes: Contradicts the common row-major default (which would give A10).

setup.title: Plate well indexing
setup.summary: How our pipelines number wells on 96-well plates.

sections.title: Order
sections.body: Our pipelines number wells 1-based in column-major order: index 1 is A1, 2 is B1, through 8 is H1, then 9 is A2, and so on down each column.

task.prompt: Under our pipeline's convention, which well label is index 10 on a 96-well plate? Answer with the label and one line of reasoning.

cases.title: Write a buffer recipe that needs a lab-standard dilution (two pages)
cases.notes: The recipe page defers the inhibitor dilution to a standards page whose value contradicts the vendor default (1:100).

setup.title: Lysis buffer L-7
setup.summary: Recipe for the standard lysis buffer.

sections.title: Recipe
sections.body: Lysis buffer L-7 is 50 mM Tris pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl and 1% NP-40, with protease inhibitor cocktail added at the lab-standard dilution.

sections.title: Protease inhibitor
sections.body: Protease inhibitor cocktail is used at 1:200, not the vendor's recommended 1:100, following the March 2026 titration.

task.prompt: Write the recipe for 10 mL of lysis buffer L-7 as a short list, including the volume of protease inhibitor cocktail to add.

cases.title: Contact the current owner after a handover (two pages, corrected)
cases.notes: The owner is reached through a team page whose lead changed.

sections.title: Responsibility
sections.body: Freezers F-1 to F-4 are maintained by the cryo team; alarms go to the cryo team lead.

sections.title: Lead
sections.body: The cryo team lead is Tomas Reyes.

sections.title: Lead
sections.body: The cryo team lead is Hanne Lie since 1 October 2026; Tomas Reyes moved to process development.

task.prompt: Freezer F-3's temperature alarm went off overnight. Write the short message I should send, addressed to the person responsible.

cases.title: Use the team's curve-fit settings, not the defaults
cases.notes: Fixed bottom, units and significant figures differ from common defaults. Checks look only at the delivered code.

setup.title: Dose-response analysis
setup.summary: How the team fits and reports dose-response curves.

sections.title: Fit
sections.body: Dose-response curves are fit with a 4-parameter logistic model with the bottom fixed at 0 and the Hill slope free. IC50 values are reported in nM to 2 significant figures.

task.prompt: Write a Python dict literal named FIT_SETTINGS with the keys model, bottom, units and sig_figs holding our team's dose-response fit settings.
